evidence.section: History of Levenshtein Distance: From Coding Theory to Modern Edit-Distance Algorithms
evidence.excerpt: The mathematical idea emerged from twentieth-century coding theory, where researchers were trying to understand how information can remain distinguishable after transmission errors. Richard Hamming developed a geometry appropriate when symbols are changed but positions remain synchronized. Fred Damerau investigated practical spelling errors involving missing, extra, incorrect, and transposed characters. Vladimir I. Levenshtein then studied communication channels in which symbols could be deleted or inserted, destroying the fixed positional correspondence on which Hamming-style reasoning depends.
